title: Lime, Ginger and Star Anise Sorbet
changes_from_base: Coconut water steeped with lime zest, lime leaves and star anise, with fresh ginger, replaces the mango purée; no corn syrup.
summary: A light, refreshing Thai-inspired sorbet of coconut water scented with lime, a little star anise and fresh ginger.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Warm gently
steps.text: Start with cold coconut water and put it in the pan with the lime zest, lime leaves and salt. Heat slowly to a bare simmer, uncovered.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Take off the heat, stir in the sugar until it dissolves, add the star anise and leave for 15 min; longer gives a stronger anise taste.

steps.title: Strain and cool
steps.text: Strain into the bowl over iced water and stir until cold.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the grated ginger and most of the lime juice, taste, and add the rest if it needs more sharpness. Chill until very cold.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min, then freeze for 1-2 h. This sorbet is light and icy, so it is best within a few days.

tips: Heat the coconut water slowly from cold so the lime aromas come out fully.
Use coconut water, not coconut milk; the result is light and clear.
Makrut lime leaves are sold fresh or frozen in Asian shops; the sorbet is still good without them.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer and eat within 3-4 days, as it becomes icy. Soften for 5 min before scooping.
